workflows.name: BOM management
workflows.trigger: A new item needs a manufacturing recipe, or an existing one changes
steps: Define BOM header for the parent item
Add component lines with quantities
Optionally add operations/routing and by-products
Validate the BOM against current component costs/checksum
Activate for use in production orders

provenance.notes: InvenTree's Part.bom_validated boolean plus validate_bom(user, valid)/is_bom_valid() methods (part/models.py, verified) give a real, if modest, two-state lifecycle: a BOM is 'draft' until a user validates it (recording a checksum + validating user/date), and becomes stale/'draft' again once components change and the stored checksum no longer matches. Neither InvenTree nor the cloned odoo-mrp scope models a richer approval workflow (e.g. pending-review, multi-step ECO); Odoo's mrp.bom has only an 'active' boolean and a 'type' select (normal/phantom), no lifecycle field. This state machine is therefore intentionally minimal rather than invented beyond the evidence.

workflows.name: Production order lifecycle
workflows.trigger: Demand (a sales order, stock shortage, or manual plan) requires building a quantity of an item
steps: Create production order for item/quantity/target date
Confirm order, reserving components
Release to the shop floor and begin production
Report progress and consume components
Mark ready to close once output is produced
Close the order, done or cancelled

provenance.notes: State names here follow Odoo's mrp.production.state verbatim (draft/confirmed/progress/to_close/done/cancel, renamed pending/confirmed/in_progress/to_close/complete/cancelled here for cross-source consistency) with an on_hold state added from InvenTree's BuildStatus.ON_HOLD, since InvenTree's own vocabulary (pending/production/on_hold/cancelled/complete) independently confirms the same overall shape. Exact event names are reasoned, not verbatim from either source.

workflows.name: Work order execution
workflows.trigger: A production order is released and its first operation becomes available
steps: Operator selects the next ready work order at their work center
Start the operation (blocked until prerequisite operations are done)
Record quantity produced as work progresses
Complete the operation, unblocking the next one
Work center becomes available for the next work order
Record scrapped/rejected quantity separately from planned output (Odoo stock.move.is_scrap / mrp.production.action_scrap)

provenance.notes: Verbatim from Odoo's mrp.workorder.state selection field and its _compute_state logic (blocked while a prerequisite blocked_by_workorder is not done/cancel, otherwise ready, then progress once qty_produced > 0); single source, InvenTree does not model this granularity. Scrap recording (manufacturing.production_scrap_tracking) is folded into this workflow rather than given its own, since scrapping happens during operation execution: Odoo has a genuine, verbatim is_scrap flag on stock.move plus mrp.production.action_scrap()/scrap_count (stock_move.py, mrp_production.py), and InvenTree has StockHistoryCode.BUILD_OUTPUT_REJECTED — two independent implementations, raising that feature to medium confidence.

workflows.name: Material requirements planning run
workflows.trigger: A scheduled or on-demand MRP run, or a reorder point is crossed
steps: Create or schedule a production plan run (manual or on a schedule)
Compute on-hand plus incoming minus demand per item against reorder points/minimum stock
For make items, add planned production quantities to the plan using the effective BOM
For buy items, add planned purchase/material-request quantities to the plan
Submit the plan to move it out of draft
Release the plan: generate production orders and/or material requests/purchase orders from it
Track the plan through to completion or closure

provenance.notes: States are verbatim from ERPNext's Production Plan doctype status field (verified via gh api), which is a genuine stateful MRP-run entity - this replaces the earlier assessment that this workflow was purely computational. Odoo's addons/mrp scope (stock.warehouse.orderpoint) and InvenTree's Part.minimum_stock/is_low_stock() corroborate the reorder-point-triggered variant of this workflow but do not themselves expose a planned-order entity with its own lifecycle; only ERPNext does. Transition event names beyond the verbatim status list are reasoned, not verbatim from ERPNext's code.

workflows.name: Quality inspection
workflows.trigger: A stock item reaches a test point defined by its part's test templates
steps: Select the test template(s)/inspection type required for the item (incoming, in-process, or outgoing)
Perform the test and record Accepted/Rejected plus any measured value
If accepted, the item proceeds (e.g. to stock or shipment)
If rejected, raise a non-conformance record
Investigate and record root cause on the non-conformance
Disposition the non-conformance (accept-as-is, rework, scrap, or return to supplier) and mark it resolved
Raise a linked corrective/preventive action (quality action) where the root cause requires a process fix
Close the corrective/preventive action once complete

provenance.notes: Accepted/Rejected/Cancelled is verbatim from ERPNext's Quality Inspection doctype status field (verified via gh api); the field's options list has a leading blank entry (no value assigned yet), reasoned here as an explicit 'pending' initial state rather than left implicit. The state machine is deliberately thin (inspection outcome is normally set once, not a multi-step transition chain) - the richer lifecycle in this workflow lives on the linked non_conformance entity (open/resolved/cancelled, see entities.json), which is where ERPNext's own CAPA process (Non Conformance -> Quality Action) actually has multiple steps. InvenTree's StockItemTestResult (boolean result) corroborates pass/fail recording generally but has no named status enum of its own.

workflows.name: Traceability lookup
workflows.trigger: A recall, customer complaint, or audit requires tracing a lot/serial forward or backward
steps: Look up the stock item's traceability records
Trace backward: which component lots/serials were consumed to produce it
Trace forward: which output lots/serials or shipments contain this component
Compile the genealogy for the audit or recall scope

provenance.notes: Deliberately left without a state_machine: a traceability lookup is a read/query operation over existing traceability_record events, not an entity with its own lifecycle - there is no 'from'/'to' status to transition through. InvenTree's StockItemTracking history and Odoo's stock.lot/mrp.production.lot_producing_ids both provide the underlying event data for this lookup. GS1 EPCIS (std:gs1-epcis, already registered in the kit's shared standards registry) is the authoritative event model (what/when/where/why) this lookup conceptually maps onto, though this domain does not yet implement or assert EPCIS-format output.

workflows.name: Manufacturing master data setup
workflows.trigger: A new item, variant, work center, stock location, or supplier needs to be onboarded before it can be used in a BOM or production order
steps: Define the item/part master record (identifiers, unit of measure, make/buy flags)
Optionally define template/variant relationships for buildable variants
Define stock locations the item will be held in
Define lot/serial tracking requirements for the item
Define or select the work center(s) that will produce the item
Define supplier records and, if purchased, link supplier parts
Define BOM substitute components and by-products where applicable

provenance.notes: This is master-data CRUD across several features rather than a single stateful process, grouped into one workflow per the research brief's guidance that 'a workflow per feature is wrong'. Each underlying model is independently corroborated in feature-map.json/entities.json; no state_machine is included because none of these are, individually, a genuinely stateful entity lifecycle.

workflows.name: Purchase requisition to goods receipt
workflows.trigger: A shortage is identified (manually, or suggested by an MRP/production-plan run) for a buy item
steps: Identify the need and select or confirm the supplier/supplier part
Create the purchase order and place it with the supplier
Supplier confirms and ships
Receive goods against the purchase order into a stock location
Optionally route received lots/serials through incoming quality inspection
Close the purchase order once fully received and reconciled, or return/cancel if rejected

provenance.notes: State machine reuses the purchase_order entity's states, verbatim from InvenTree's PurchaseOrderStatus enum (see entities.json). ERPNext's independently-named Purchase Order status field (Draft/On Hold/To Receive and Bill/To Bill/To Receive/Completed/Cancelled/Closed/Delivered) corroborates the same overall shape with a different, more billing-oriented vocabulary; not merged in to avoid presenting a blended enum as verbatim. Transition event names are reasoned.

workflows.name: Subcontract operation execution
workflows.trigger: A production order includes an operation that must be performed by an external supplier
steps: Create a subcontract order for the operation, referencing the production order
Transfer the required components/materials to the subcontractor
Subcontractor performs the operation
Receive the finished or semi-finished output back into stock (fully or partially)
Optionally inspect the received output
Close the subcontract order once fully received

provenance.notes: States are verbatim from ERPNext's Subcontracting Order status field (verified via gh api). InvenTree only models this as a boolean (Build.external), with no distinct order lifecycle, so InvenTree corroborates the concept of subcontracting but not this specific state machine.

workflows.name: Equipment maintenance
workflows.trigger: A preventive maintenance schedule comes due, or a work center reports a problem/blocked state
steps: Schedule preventive maintenance for a work center/asset, or log a corrective request when a problem is reported
Take the work center out of production (blocked/maintenance state)
Perform the maintenance task and log parts/time used
Record completion
Return the work center to service (normal/production state)

provenance.notes: Steps are reasoned from Odoo's mrp.workcenter.working_state/blocked_time/productive_time computed fields and ERPNext's Maintenance Schedule (status: Draft/Submitted/Cancelled) plus Asset Maintenance/Asset Maintenance Log doctypes (verified via gh api). No state_machine is included: ERPNext's Maintenance Schedule status is the generic Frappe submittable-document pattern (draft/submitted/cancelled), not a maintenance-specific lifecycle, and neither source models a richer preventive/corrective task lifecycle worth asserting as verbatim.

workflows.name: Disassembly / unbuild
workflows.trigger: A completed (or partially completed) production order's output needs to be broken back down into components, e.g. for rework or reclaiming parts
steps: Select the production order/stock item to unbuild
Create an unbuild/disassembly record referencing the quantity to reverse
Move recovered components back into stock at a destination location
Mark the unbuild record done

provenance.notes: The draft/done states are verbatim from Odoo's mrp.unbuild.state selection field (mrp_unbuild.py). This is modeled here as reusing the production_order entity for simplicity (an unbuild order is conceptually the reverse of a production order); Odoo actually implements mrp.unbuild as its own doctype/model, not a state of mrp.production itself - noted as a simplification, not a claim that InvenTree/Odoo share one literal table for this. InvenTree's StockHistoryCode.DISASSEMBLED/CREATED_FROM_DISASSEMBLY corroborates the general capability without its own state enum.

workflows.name: Stocktake / cycle counting
workflows.trigger: A scheduled or ad-hoc physical inventory count is due for a location or item
steps: Schedule a count for a location, category, or item
Operator physically counts on-hand quantity, typically scanning barcodes
System compares counted quantity to system on-hand quantity
Variances above a threshold are reviewed/approved
Stock quantity is adjusted to match the count

provenance.notes: InvenTree's PartStocktake model (stocktake_date/stocktake_user fields) and ERPNext's Stock Reconciliation doctype (confirmed to exist via gh api tree listing; a dedicated physical-count/variance-reconciliation entity) independently corroborate this process. No state_machine included: neither source's count/reconciliation record exposes a named status enum beyond the generic Frappe draft/submitted/cancelled document pattern for ERPNext, which was not judged worth asserting as domain-specific.

workflows.name: Production cost rollup and capacity reporting
workflows.trigger: A production order completes an operation or closes, or a planner needs to review work center load
steps: Accumulate material cost from components consumed
Accumulate labor cost from work center hourly rate x actual operation time
Roll material and labor cost up onto the produced item's cost
Visualize work center load (queued/in-progress/blocked/late work orders) across the plan horizon
Flag late or over-capacity work centers for replanning

provenance.notes: Steps are reasoned from Odoo's mrp.workcenter.costs_hour (labor cost basis) and computed workorder_count/workorder_ready_count/workorder_progress_count/workorder_blocked_count/workorder_late_count fields. ISA-95/IEC 62264's Production Capability model (which includes equipment capacity as a named element) corroborates capacity as a standard concept, not an implementation. No cited source models a complete cost-rollup or capacity-planning UI end to end, so this is reported as reasoned/computational, not backed by a full verbatim implementation; no state_machine (this is a recurring computation/report, not an entity lifecycle).
